si_thresholds: abnormal ECG (arrhythmia, conduction abnormality, or ischemic changes)
elevated troponin in appropriate clinical context
high-risk features: age over 60, no prodrome, exertional onset, family history of sudden death
injury from fall (head trauma, fracture, significant bleeding)
persistent orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, or tachycardia
is_requirements: continuous telemetry monitoring for suspected arrhythmic etiology
serial troponins when cardiac etiology suspected
advanced diagnostics (echocardiography, stress testing, EP study, tilt-table)
two_midnight_expectation: Highly variable; published validation found criteria predict stays over two midnights poorly in elderly syncope (sensitivity 60.8%, specificity 47.8%; median stay 32.6 hours). High-risk patients may require multi-day monitoring.
denial_downgrade_triggers: vasovagal syncope with clear trigger and rapid recovery
single episode with normal ECG, normal troponin, no high-risk features
orthostatic hypotension without a cardiac etiology
overturn_support_factors: documented cardiac risk (abnormal ECG, structural disease, exertional onset, family history)
documented fall injury or recurrent falls with gait instability
age and frailty raising adverse-outcome risk and monitoring need
recurrent syncope or multiple ED visits indicating high readmission risk

citations.source: Journal of Emergency Medicine (Chang et al., accuracy of criteria for observation vs inpatient in older adults with syncope)
